title: mini-fanout-tilt-with-quarantine-checkpoint-and-autoremediation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Some customers run tightly-coupled model swap flows where sudden promotes cause transient regressions that escape existing canary windows. This PR introduces a 'mini fanout tilt' rollout primitive: a phased, micro-fanout promotion lane that enforces an integrity sample checkpoint (quarantine) before increasing live traffic, and an autoremediation policy that can instant-revert the promote when defined telemetry deterioration patterns are observed. The goal is to reduce blast radius for small, high-risk promotes while keeping promotion latency low for safe workloads. Summary of changes: 1) rollout/controller: add MiniFanoutTiltController with stage definitions: seed (0.5% traffic), probe (2%), tilt (5%), steady (100%), each stage having a quarantine_checkpoint where a sampled subset of requests are validated against integrity probes and a secondary shadow pipeline. 2) policy/rollback: add AutoremediatePolicy that binds to metric predicates (latency/err_rate/regression_delta) with hysteresis and soft-threshold windows to avoid flapping; supports configurable quarantine duration and holdpoints. 3) telemetry: new integrity.metrics and a sampled integrity probe trace that correlates shadow vs live outputs for drift/regression detection. 4) router: lightweight fanout adapter that can split and tag traffic for quarantine and shadow lanes with minimal overhead. 5) console: expose per-stage SLO gauges and a 'quarantine preview' view for operators. 6) e2e and unit tests plus quickstart docs and rollout examples. Checklist: - [x] Implement controller and policy - [x] Unit tests for controller transitions - [x] Integration tests with synthetic traffic harness - [x] Console and docs updates - [x] Perf microbench and latency impact under 2% at p95 - [x] Add Linear links and playbook notes Related work: builds on ENG-4302 (shadow verifier) and ENG-5610 (staged canary hooks). Rollout semantics: the controller performs micro-commits between stages and writes a lightweight checkpoint to the rollout ledger. During quarantine_checkpoint, a sampled 1k requests are run through parallel shadow pipeline and evaluated by integrity probes before proceeding. Autoremediate triggers a deterministic revert if configured predicates hold for configured windows. Backwards compatibility: default policies are off; existing rollouts continue to work. Notes on operational safety: quarantine is a read-only passive verification by default; when enabled operators can opt-in auto-commit or manual-approve at quarantine exit. Implementation details and decisions: to keep latency impact minimal, fanout tagging occurs in the ingress path and sampling uses an LRU token cache to avoid extra synchronous calls. Hysteresis windows are implemented using sliding-window counters rather than histograms to keep memory bounded at scale. Metrics surfaced: fanout.quarantine.sample_rate, fanout.quarantine.pass_ratio, autoremediate.trigger_count, rollout.stage_duration_seconds, integrity.shadow_discrepancy_rate. Migration: no DB migrations required; ledger entries are an additional column in the rollout table with default null for older rows. Playbook excerpt added to docs/release-playbooks/mini-fanout-tilt.md with step-by-step recovery and contact points.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can you clarify why you chose sliding-window counters instead of histograms? Concern about lost resolution for tail latency signals.

Maya Chen: Sliding windows keep memory predictable at scale; histograms were too heavy for hot-path and introduce more CPU overhead. We added a lightweight p99 probe in telemetry for tail-sensitive predicates.
Priya Nair: Need explicit test for flapping prevention — ensure autoremediate won't oscillate on marginal spikes.
Maya Chen: Added integration test 'autoremediate_flap_protection' that injects transient spikes and verifies hysteresis avoids revert. See tests/integration/tilt_harness.yaml commit.
Ethan Walters: Console UX looks good; add a tooltip explaining sampled counts and confidence intervals.
Maya Chen: Tooltip added and copy reviewed by UX; included link to docs that explain statistical power for the quarantine sample.

release_notes: Introduce 'Mini Fanout Tilt' rollout primitive: phased micro-fanout promotion with quarantine checkpoint and optional autoremediation for automatic revert on detector-defined regressions. Operators can enable per-rollout. See docs/release-playbooks/mini-fanout-tilt.md for playbook and examples.
